text:
Distance to Earth  
Large Magellanic Cloud ≈ 1.6 × 10⁵ light-years  

Speed of the spacecraft  
v = 0.999 999 87 c

1. Lorentz factor γ  
1 – v²/c² = 1 – (0.999 999 87)² ≈ 2.6 × 10⁻⁷  
γ = 1 / √(1 – v²/c²) ≈ 1 / √(2.6 × 10⁻⁷) ≈ 1 / (5.1 × 10⁻⁴) ≈ 1.96 × 10³

2. Time to cover the distance in the rest (Earth/LMC) frame  
t = (distance) / v ≈ (1.6 × 10⁵ ly)/c ≈ 1.6 × 10⁵ years  
(the factor 1/v differs from 1 by only 1.3 × 10⁻⁷, negligible here)

3. Proper time experienced by the astronaut  
τ = t / γ ≈ (1.6 × 10⁵ yr) / (1.96 × 10³) ≈ 8.2 × 10¹ yr ≈ 82 yr

Thus the astronaut feels about 8 × 10¹ years elapse on board.  
Starting at age 22, arrival age ≈ 22 + 82 ≈ 104 years, well within their 150-year lifespan.

Closest choice: 81 years.

Answer: A
